Grm1: alpha / beta RNA and splice evidence

Twelve P60 mice · six WT and six Satb2 cKO · frozen Seurat populations · superficial CA1 C2+C3 · deep CA1 C1+C5 · original inhibitory clusters

Six annotated RNA models encode two receptor protein forms. Three coding transcripts map to alpha (201) or beta (202/203); three additional models are noncoding. This 10x nuclear RNA analysis distinguishes diagnostic feature support, conservative splice-supported assignments and overlapping transcript-compatible upper bounds. Shared reads are not arbitrarily divided. Zero support does not prove biological absence.

Why only 15 α-associated UMIs in C2 and one in C6?

Gene-level Grm1 abundance and evidence for a processed α or β transcript answer different questions. Totals below sum the twelve mice. Most gene UMIs include intronic evidence; shared exons also cannot identify an isoform. These categories overlap and must not be added.

EvidenceIN C2IN C6
All Grm1 gene UMIs16,5643,698
UMIs with intronic evidence15,5033,447
UMIs with exonic evidence1,102266
UMIs with compatible anchored splice evidence12536
α-diagnostic feature UMIs425101
Conservative α-associated RNA UMIs151
Direct α-discriminating terminal-junction UMIs20

The 15 and 1 are conservative RNA-support counts, not α abundance estimates or numbers of α-positive nuclei. Assignment requires family-specific feature evidence, compatibility with the α model, a compatible anchored splice and no incompatible anchored splice. The splice need not be the α-discriminating tail junction. Direct tail-junction support is only two in C2 and zero in C6. Zero β support and sparse α support do not establish absence, an α/β ratio or a genotype-dependent isoform switch.

Validation priority: use α-skip and β-exon-inclusion junction RT-PCR on independently identified C2/C6-like cells, sequence the amplicons, then quantify with validated junction-specific RT-qPCR or RT-ddPCR across mice. Check assays against all six reference RNA models; a region coding only in α can be transcribed as β UTR and is not automatically α-specific. Include DNase, no-RT, no-template and cloned α/β specificity controls. Targeted long-read cDNA can resolve connected transcript structures. Confirm protein with validated C-terminal α/β antibodies and Grm1-knockout controls in identified cells.

Per-animal evidence

Appearance and feature selection

Blue and rust headers identify WT and cKO. Every column is one mouse. Color uses log(1 + displayed value); its limit is recomputed for the displayed panel. Feature rows can overlap and must not be summed as gene totals. A gray dash means the population was not sampled in that mouse.

Alpha/beta annotations and strength of support

Grm1-201 → mGluR1 alpha (1199 aa). Grm1-202 and -203 encode identical mGluR1 beta (906 aa) proteins with different UTRs. Grm1-204/-205/-206 are noncoding models. Shared beta reads are counted once at the protein-family level and are not arbitrarily split between transcript IDs.

Conservative alpha/beta counts are uniquely compatible with a protein family, diagnostic and splice-supported; they are evidence lower bounds, not full-length abundance estimates. Replicated support (≥3 UMIs in ≥2 mice) is a descriptive flag, not a hypothesis test.

In Ferraguti et al. 1998, Figure 4B is a hippocampal synaptosome protein blot: alpha ~150 kDa and beta ~97 kDa. “4B” is a panel label, not an isoform or gene name. The blot does not identify the contributing cell types. Grm7 encodes the separate mGlu7A/B receptors.

Counts use primary MAPQ255, exclusive Grm1 assignment, corrected CB/UB, mm≠1 and xf bits 2/4/32 excluded. Junctions require at least eight contiguous aligned bases on both sides. Original nucleus identities and all earlier analyses remain unchanged.

Protein context: Ferraguti et al. 1998 · Techlovská et al. 2014. This analysis measures nuclear RNA features; receptor protein abundance, trafficking and electrophysiology were not measured.
